customManagers.description: Versions pinned in workflow with: blocks, annotated with a renovate datasource comment.
Registry-qualified Docker images pinned as repository-local composite-action input defaults.

packageRules.description: Automerge everything except major updates

Hold pnpm off 11.12.0: that release regressed pnpm's own global self-installer (createFullPkgId throws 'Cannot use in operator to search for integrity in undefined'), so pnpm/action-setup crashes during CI setup the moment a repo bumps its packageManager field to it. The range allows every other version, so Renovate resumes bumping as soon as a fixed patch (11.12.1+) ships — drop this rule then.

Hold TypeScript on the v6 line until the toolchain supports the v7 native-compiler rewrite. TS7 removes JS-API surface prettier's .ts-config loader relies on (it reads an undefined ModuleKind member and throws), and typescript-eslint still caps its peer range at typescript <6.1.0, so a frozen-lockfile install fails on the unmet peer. Drop this rule once typescript-eslint's peer range admits v7.

Hold golangci-lint off v2.13.0: its bundled nilness analyzer panics on valid service code with 'internal error: unhandled builtin recover', so both Renovate artifact generation and lint-go fail. The range admits every other release, so Renovate resumes on the first fixed patch — drop this rule then.

Hold google.golang.org/grpc off v1.84.0 because CVE-2026-84445 is reported in that release while v1.83.2 remains fixed. The range admits every other release, so Renovate resumes on the first fixed stable patch — drop this rule then.

Hold GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runners below v26 until GitHub Actions offers the ubuntu-26.04 label. Renovate currently derives it from runner metadata even though actionlint and GitHub reject the unavailable label — drop this rule once the runner is generally available.

Give GitHub releases time to finish publishing binary assets and checksums before CI installs them. Apply the same delay to all release-backed tools instead of maintaining version-specific exceptions.

Match pnpm's minimumReleaseAge supply-chain gate, scoped to the npm manager (which is what Renovate uses for pnpm: pnpm-lock.yaml, workspaces, catalogs) so it doesn't open/rebase PRs for packages too fresh to pass pnpm install. Other ecosystems (gomod, docker, github-actions) aren't gated by pnpm, so they keep landing security patches without delay. Keep >= pnpm's value (defined in nodelib-config).
Bump the main go directive, grouped with the golang base image. Tool modfiles keep their existing compatibility floor until a tool dependency requires a newer Go release.

Keep the golang base image in the same PR as the go directive. Renovate runs the branch's artifact updates with the config of its first upgrade by depName, which is this image, so it carries go.mod's tidy.

Keep every Google Terraform provider constraint and lockfile update in one PR. Pinning reusable modules separately from root provider upgrades leaves the roots locked to a version that no longer satisfies those modules.
Keep workflows action and Renovate preset refs on the same release in one update PR.

Move every Bun module in one PR. Bun panics at init unless its dialect matches the core version, yet the core module does not require its dialects, so tidy never raises them. Services import pgdialect only through golib, which leaves it `// indirect` and disabled by Renovate's gomod manager unless this rule enables it.

Consolidate non-major npm updates into one PR per repo. They all edit the shared pnpm-lock.yaml, so as separate PRs they conflict pairwise and the merge queue can only land one per cycle. This rule follows the recommended preset so it supersedes its per-name and monorepo groups; exact fleet rules below may override it.

Ship each service's Go module, npm client and images in one PR, since the module must match its images. Renovate runs every artifact update with the config of the branch's first upgrade by depName, usually an image, so each member carries the options its siblings need; the rules follow the npm catch-all so the client keeps its group.
Keep the pre-1.0 uikit package family together and require review because minor releases may break consumers.
Keep Playwright packages and CI container images on the same runtime version. The image sorts first and lends the branch its artifact config, so the group carries npm's dedupe.
Keep the Vitest core and scoped packages on one runnable version.
Keep Vite and the Svelte Vite plugin on a compatible release line.

Leave pnpm audit-managed overrides to the audit action. node-actions/audit runs `pnpm audit --fix=override` daily and pins vulnerable transitive dependencies to the minimal patched version within each consumer's supported range. Renovate's npm manager otherwise re-reads the override value as an ordinary dependency and bumps it to the latest major, pushing the pin past the parent's compatibility ceiling (e.g. undici v8 breaks jsdom's private wrap-handler.js deep-import). Audit owns these values; Renovate must not touch them. All three depTypes must stay listed: Renovate types package.json `pnpm.overrides` and its `overrides` alias, but overrides declared in pnpm-workspace.yaml (pnpm 10's preferred location) get `pnpm-workspace.overrides` — omit it and the guard silently no-ops for every workspace-level override.
